title: Kitewing Commerce — outbound play & research
content:
Snapshot: quick research + outbound sequence for Kitewing Commerce (mid-market omnichannel retailer). Notes for first-touch cadences, personas, technical integration signal, pricing anchor and objections. Work-in-progress — meant for SDR + AE pairing.

Account summary:
- Company: Kitewing Commerce (brand: kitewing.com — storefront + marketplace integration).
- HQ: Portland, OR (series B, ~230 employees).
- FY revenue estimate: $180M–260M (public signals + press).
- Why they matter: aggressive personalization roadmap; engineering blog posts about headless storefront and search relevance experiments in 2024. Potential fit for Redwood: embeddings for search & product recommendation, hosted API for experiments, Dedicated for predictable peak BFCM throughput.

Signals & tech fit (quick hits):
- Uses Kubernetes on GCP (job postings show k8s + Terraform).
- Open-source search + vector store mentioned in blog (signals willingness to integrate embeddings).
- Heavy emphasis on latency for search/autocomplete (slim margins for UX).
- They list "A/B & feature flags" as core to product development — good for canaries / gradual rollout messaging.

Key contacts (prioritized):
1) Morgan Hayes — VP Product (product@kitewing.com) — owns personalization & search. LinkedIn: product → head of personalization hires 2023; presents at retail-tech meetup. Likely receptive to experimentation + POV on model/regression guardrails.
2) Diego Ramos — Head of Platform/Infra — LinkedIn shows previous infra role at a scale SaaS; interested in cost predictability and private deployments. Decision influence: Dedicated vs private.
3) Priyanka Mehta — Engineering manager, Relevance team — day-to-day owner for embeddings + ranking infra. Good technical champion.
4) Casey Lin — Director of Data Science — evaluation lead for quality metrics; cares about drift and reproducible evals.

Primary pain / opportunity framing:
- Current pain: slow turnaround on search relevance experiments; high cost of in-house embedding infra (ops overhead); need predictable latency during campaigns and holiday peaks.
- Opportunity to pitch: Redwood reduces operational cost, offers predictable latency SLOs, provides built-in eval tooling to detect regressions (appeals to data science). Emphasize routing & fallback to cheaper quantized models during peaks to control cost.

Suggested outbound sequence (multi-channel) — 6 touch framework (email + LinkedIn + call):
- Touch 1 (Email, Subject lines options):
  * "Quick Q — personalization latency at Kitewing"
  * "One way to reduce embedding costs for Kitewing"
  Snippet: "Morgan — saw Kitewing's post on relevance experiments. We helped a retail customer drop embedding infra ops by 70% and cut tail-latency during promos — curious if that's relevant?"

- Touch 2 (LinkedIn DM if connection available):
  * Short: "Loved your talk at PDX Retail Tech — one note: we saw big wins by adding prefix KV caching plus a canary fallback to a smaller quantized model — happy to share numbers. — Ethan"

- Touch 3 (Value email w/ data):
  * Attach short two-slide PDF: "Kitewing quick win — estimate" with cost/latency projection (back-of-envelope).

- Touch 4 (Call/Voicemail):
  * Voicemail script: "Hi Morgan, Ethan at Redwood — two minutes to share a concrete experiment that reduced embedding cost while keeping NDCG stable. Drop me a time?"

- Touch 5 (Technical note to Diego):
  * Subject: "Architectural note — Dedicated pools + burst strategy for BFCM"
  * Snippet: "Diego — curious if you have reserved capacity today for peak events. We can show how Dedicated + autoscaling burst keeps P99 latency under X ms while matching cost targets."

- Touch 6 (Breakup + offer to help):
  * Subject: "One last thing on Kitewing — offer to share test data"
  * Snippet: "If useful, we can run a 48–72 hr pilot against a small test set (no long contract) to show delta on latency/cost/quality."

Playbook for AE + Solutions (quick bullets):
- First call goal: qualify relevance metric (what they track: MRR lift? A/B? click-through?). Ask for: existing embedding dimensionality, vector store choice, current avg and P99 latencies for search calls.
- Demo plan: show 2 charts — (1) token-level latency vs sequence length across model variants, (2) cost per 1M queries w/ caching & batching. Keep to 15 min technical + 15 min decision makers.
- Pilot approach: 2-week focused pilot (hosted) -> measure latency, cost, and NDCG on their labelled queries. If they want data residency, transition to Dedicated or Private with same configuration.

Objection handling (anticipated):
- "We already built embeddings in-house": acknowledge + ask about ops cost and time-to-experiment. Pitch Redwood's batching & KV prefix cache as additive, highlights reduced engineering time to maintain.
- "Security / data residency concerns": default move to Private or Dedicated with KMS integration; share SOC2 + audit artifacts (link to security page in artifact list).
- "Pricing unknown / unpredictable": show committed Dedicated pricing vs hosted usage. Offer a short benchmark test with a cost projection and a 1–month committed burst cap to bound spend.
- "Quality/regression risk": highlight Redwood Optimize + evals tied to prompt sets — built-in regression alerts and manual rollback / canary. Offer to run candidate comparisons on their sample queries during pilot.

Pricing anchor (quick sketch for internal use):
- Experimental hosted pilot: free (limited) + discounted token/embedding rates for pilot window.
- Post-pilot options: Hosted pay-as-you-go; Dedicated monthly commitment starting at ~$45k/month for small pool (estimate — need confirm). Private (on-prem/VPC) licensed + deployment fee.
- Note: aim to get commitment to POC with clear success metrics rather than negotiate final pricing on first outreach.

Integration checklist (tech notes for SE):
- Need small dataset: 5–10k labeled queries + sample embedding pipeline output.
- Endpoint access patterns: search/autocomplete vs batch offline ranking. Identify both.
- Security: confirm SSO + SCIM for pilot users, KMS requirement for keys, any SOC2 requirements.

Open questions / next actions (TODOs):
- [ ] Priya to draft two-slide cost/latency estimate by 2025-11-18.
- [ ] Lucas to source 10 representative queries + labels from Kitewing public demo or common product categories.
- [ ] Set intro call with Morgan (target: 2025-11-24). Priya to own calendar outreach.
- [ ] Prepare short technical appendix for Diego on Dedicated autoscaling behavior (SE note).

Quick internal notes / heuristics for AEs: keep outreach concise, call out concrete metric wins (latency in ms, cost %), and always offer a low-risk pilot. Avoid heavy product marketing — lean on engineering signals and numbers.

Scratch ideas (brainstorm, informal):
- Could propose a "holiday readiness" short program: run a free stress test on a week of traffic replay to show tail latency improvements.
- Offer a co-marketing case study if pilot converts (headline: "Kitewing increases conversion by X% while lowering embedding costs").
- If they are hesitant about Dedicated, propose a hybrid: hosted for experiments + dedicated reserved capacity during BFCM for production.

Notes to self:
- Morgan seemed to like vendor partners that provide reproducible evals. Bring example eval dashboards.
- Diego will ask about GPU types. Have quick reference: A100 vs H100 cost/latency tradeoffs + quantized CPU fallback notes.

Last edited: 2025-12-03 by Ethan Morales.

End of notes.
